reviews.body: Column change is right, but we shouldn't convert back to float in Python. Details inline.
Thanks, Decimal all the way through looks good.

comments.author: bob
comments.body:
Float will bite us here even with a numeric column. `asdecimal=False` hands the value back to Python as a float, so every sum in settlement goes through binary floating point again and we're back to the 0.01 drift finance found. Same for `round(amount, 2)` in the service: `round(2.675, 2)` is 2.67, not 2.68.

Please drop `asdecimal=False`, type these as `Mapped[Decimal]`, and have the services take and return `Decimal` (quantize to `Decimal("0.01")` on the way in). The API schema can keep accepting JSON numbers for now, pydantic will coerce.

comments.author: carol
comments.body: I kept float to avoid touching every call site, but you're right that it only moves the problem. There are only three callers of create_charge, I'll switch them.

comments.author: carol
comments.body: Done: Decimal in the model and services, quantize in create_charge, tests updated.
